body.prose:
Where the reader looks is the page's address, so going back and forward is only the address changing, and a reload lands where the address says. What the reader has looked at is kept in the home as their history, a holon each move adds a visit to and nothing rewrites; the root mount holds only what is the reader's, the component it calls and what it offers, and no longer changes with every move.

*Reasoned, the session's, 2026-11-01, answering the author's question of what a virtual history stack means; the root's versions were the history from 2026-11-03 until the author found, the next day, that walking back by writing old versions again is not real history, since commits are a line you can't reverse. As [the interface](ref:01M6JZY20ZJAAP3CBJ4KRDBXFD) tells.*
body.title: The history is a holon of its own
